defaults.permitted_development: Across County County Durham, roof-lights are often permitted development where they stay low-profile, project no more than 150mm from the roof plane and do not rise above the existing roof height. The straightforward route can disappear if the property is listed, subject to local restrictions or if the proposal starts to read as a roof enlargement rather than a simple skylight.

rules.height_rules: Across County County Durham, a roof-light must not push the roof above the existing highest part. Keeping the frame low-profile and subordinate to the roof slope is usually the safest approach.
rules.depth_rules: Across County County Durham, depth is controlled by projection from the roof plane rather than by the size of the opening alone. Once the unit projects more than 150mm, the straightforward householder route is usually lost.
rules.boundary_rules: Across County County Durham, boundary impact usually comes through privacy rather than distance. Side-facing roof-light windows should be obscure-glazed and, if openable, the opening part should have its lowest point at least 1.7 metres above the room floor.
rules.roof_rules: Across County County Durham, roof-lights are treated as minor roof alterations, not full roof enlargements, so the existing roof form should remain dominant. Roof terraces, raised platforms and larger roof additions sit outside the normal roof-light route.
rules.materials_rules: Across County County Durham, the best material strategy is usually visual restraint. Low-profile frames and clean flashings that work with the existing roof covering are less likely to jar with the roofscape than chunky or highly contrasting units.

restrictions.conservation_area: A roof-light in a conservation area is usually easiest to justify when it is discreetly placed and does not disrupt an established roof form.
restrictions.listed_building: A listed building roof usually needs a heritage-led approach: even a small roof-light can require consent if it affects the historic fabric or appearance.
restrictions.article4_notes: A local Article 4 direction or earlier planning condition can take away the normal roof-light permitted development route, particularly on prominent roof slopes.

rules.permitted_development: In Darlington, roof-lights are often permitted development where they stay low-profile, project no more than 150mm from the roof plane and do not rise above the existing roof height. The straightforward route can disappear if the property is listed, subject to local restrictions or if the proposal starts to read as a roof enlargement rather than a simple skylight.

rules.height_rules: The alteration must not exceed the height of the existing roof. In practice that means choosing a low-profile unit that sits quietly within the roof slope rather than reading as an added structure on top of it.
rules.depth_rules: Depth is controlled by projection from the roof plane rather than by the size of the opening alone. Once the unit projects more than 150mm, the straightforward householder route is usually lost.
rules.boundary_rules: Roof-lights do not have a normal setback rule, but side-facing windows can still affect neighbours. Obscure glazing and a 1.7 metre minimum level to any opening part are the usual privacy conditions.
rules.roof_rules: The proposal should read as a modest alteration to the existing roof rather than a new roof form in its own right. Roof terraces and larger enlargements are separate development types with stricter rules.
rules.materials_rules: Materials are not just about weathering: they control how visible the roof-light looks. Neat flashings, restrained frame colours and a low-profile unit usually sit better than bright trims or bulky cassettes.

restrictions.conservation_area: Conservation area status makes roof-lights more sensitive on visible elevations, particularly where a simple modern unit would cut across a traditional roof pattern.
restrictions.listed_building: Listed building consent may be required for roof-lights where the work alters historic roof fabric, framing, coverings or the character of the building.
restrictions.article4_notes: A local Article 4 direction or earlier planning condition can take away the normal roof-light permitted development route, particularly on prominent roof slopes.
